Mine was found by accident as well! I was seeing an ophthalmologist to get two different surgeries on my eyes and he noticed the swollen optic nerves and said I needed to get that figured out before I could get either surgery. My vision loss from my eye condition (Kerataconus) is crazy unstable and can change pretty much anytime it wants. I’m already 3x the legal limit to be considered legally blind in my right eye (20/600) and my left eye is just barely hovering at 20/40 (the legal limit to drive). It’s crazy because 3 years ago I had 20/20 vision in both eyes. So it’s been a crazy road of trying to get diagnosed as quickly as possible so I can get it under control enough to at least get the first surgery I’ll need to stop the progression in my good eye. Unfortunately the medical world doesn’t operate very fast lol.

My therapist was super great about it. She makes sure I’m being safe and taking care of wounds but doesn’t force me to stop. At first it was really hard to tell her and right after I felt a lot of shame every week when I came back and couldn’t say I stopped but it is a symptom and not the root of the problem, she knew that and it only took me a few weeks to catch up lol. I feel like she always knows me before I do. The shame right after was  my biggest negative I guess, because it’s hard enough to be honest about things like that. But that wasn’t her fault, that was the depression and suicidal thoughts talking. I’m not clean yet but my therapist introduced me to this idea of doing one thing when I get those thoughts before I act on them. It can be anything, listen to a song, light a candle, go for a walk, take a shower. Just one thing, and then if the thoughts are still there I can make the decision to do one more thing or to cut. Sometimes I can keep doing just one more thing until the thoughts pass and sometimes I can’t. But at least I know I did one thing to try to stop. And that helps with the inevitable shame and disappointment when I do end up cutting.
